mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained return to out-of-home activities, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards as more people engage in public life.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their upward trend, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility (from -31.7 to -21.1) signals a strong return to offices. If this trend continues and WORKPLACES crosses -20%, it will directly stimulate nearby retail and recreation.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -20% from baseline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not improve compared to the last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with the steady increase in TRANSIT usage indicates a fundamental shift in daily routines, with people spending less time at home and more time commuting, leading to increased opportunities for retail and recreation.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and TRANSIT continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The observed broad-based increase in mobility across most categories (WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, GROCERY_PHARM) suggests an underlying policy environment of easing restrictions. This policy stance will continue to encourage out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: Government policy announcements indicate a reversal or tightening of restrictions, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite stable easing policies.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility (from -12.3 to -21.4) suggests a reduction in outdoor leisure activities, possibly due to changing weather or public sentiment. This shift could divert discretionary time and spending away from general recreation, negatively impacting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility falls by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM mobility at a near-baseline level (-1.7%) indicates that essential shopping patterns have largely normalized. This stability suggests a baseline level of public comfort and activity, which will allow for further growth in non-essential RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within 2 percentage points of baseline
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains stable near baseline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days declines.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a strong rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, RETAIL_REC showed a slight decline in the last week. This suggests that increased work-related movement is not fully translating into retail activity, possibly due to continued remote work or economic caution, leading to a negative impact on RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RETAIL_REC falls week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises while RETAIL_REC falls week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days significantly increases.

mechanism_narrative: After a period of recovery, RETAIL_REC mobility has plateaued or slightly declined in the most recent week (-23.4 to -22.7). This indicates that the initial surge of activity post-lockdown may be losing momentum, suggesting a short-term slowdown or reversal.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change is less than 1 percentage point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC plateaus or slightly declines, but then significantly increases in the following week.
